title: Construct Binary Tree From Preorder And Inorder Traversal
statement: You get two lists that came from the same binary tree with all-different values: its preorder walk (node, left, right) and its inorder walk (left, node, right). Rebuild the tree and return its root.

example.caption: Preorder starts with the root 3. Inorder puts 9 on its left and 15, 20, 7 on its right.

idea.sentence: Preorder tells you each root in turn, and the root's position in inorder splits the values into a left part and a right part.

jargon.plain: Visit the node first, then the whole left subtree, then the whole right subtree. The first value is always the root.
Visit the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. Values left of the root in this list are exactly its left subtree.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the preorder list and the inorder list, e.g. [3,9,20,15,7] and [9,3,15,20,7]

compare.bruteLabel: Search inorder for the root every time
compare.optimalLabel: Look the root up in a map
compare.unit: steps (a tree that is a long chain)

rows.name: Scan for the root
rows.note: Each node scans the inorder list to find its root position. The space is the call stack.

rows.name: Value to index map
rows.note: The map costs O(n) once. Then every node finds its split in one lookup.

fast.takeaway: Preorder gives roots in order. One map from value to inorder position turns each split into a single lookup.

stages.title: Index inorder
stages.note: Store each value's position in inorder in a map. Keep a pointer next into preorder, starting at 0.

stages.title: Take the root
stages.note: The value at next in preorder is the root of the current inorder window. Move next forward and look up the root's position.

stages.title: Build the left subtree
stages.note: The window part to the left of the root belongs to the left subtree. Build it first, because preorder lists the left side first.

stages.title: Build the right subtree
stages.note: The window part to the right of the root belongs to the right subtree. Build it second.

stages.title: Return the root
stages.note: The outer call returns the root of the whole tree.

edges.title: Empty lists
edges.why: The window is empty from the start, so the first call returns null.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: The root splits an empty left part and an empty right part. Both calls return null at once.

edges.title: Left chain
edges.why: Each root sits at the right end of its window, so the right part is empty every time.

edges.title: Right chain
edges.why: Each root sits at the left end of its window, so the left part is empty every time.

gotchas.text: Build the left subtree before the right. Preorder lists the left values first, so next has to walk through them in that order.
Slicing the arrays for each call works but costs O(n) per call. Pass index bounds (lo, hi) instead, and keep one shared next pointer.
This only works when all values are different. With duplicates a value no longer names one position in inorder.
next must live outside the recursive function and be incremented inside it. A parameter would be copied and the left call's progress would be lost.
Recursive closures need the var build func(...) declaration first, then the assignment. Writing build := func... cannot call itself.

recap.key: Preorder gives the next root. Its inorder position splits the window into left and right. Build left, then right.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(n) for the map.
moves: Map each inorder value to its index
Left = build(lo, mid-1). Right = build(mid+1, hi)
